summary: A 100-foot Aermotor LS-40 tower from the 1940s or 1950s, used until the 1980s; its cab has been removed and it is privately owned.

facts.status_note: The cab has been removed; the tower structure was still standing as of 2022.

access.note: Privately owned; the register does not describe public access.

events.note: Register notes the tower structure still standing and its cab removed
Registered as NHLR US 1703 (NC 29) on December 25, 2022

evidence.supports: 100-foot Aermotor LS-40; built 1940s or 1950s; active until 1980s; no exact year given
evidence.quote: This 100-foot Aermotor LS-40 was built sometime in the 1940s or 1950s and actively used until the 1980s.

evidence.supports: tower structure still standing as of 2022; cab removed
evidence.quote: The tower structure is still standing as of 2022, but its cab has been removed.
The tower is now privately owned.

sources.title: Currituck Fire Tower
sources.publisher: National Historic Lookout Register (American Resources, Inc. and Forest Fire Lookout Association)

notes_for_editor: Single source: the NHLR register entry, which dates the tower only to the 1940s or 1950s and gives no removal date for the cab. The record's agency field names the private owner; the story does not repeat the name because it is not needed. The record's ownership field is unknown and could read private per the register; it was left unchanged. Record status standing is consistent with the structure still standing in 2022, but the status_note records the cab removal. Access is private, so the story asks visitors not to climb without permission. A FFLA Aermotor booklet was found but did not yield text, so the LS-40 design is taken from the register alone. Two WebSearch queries and four reads were used.
